steps: Entered seed CO-UKR-MAYA1 via Play a seed
Picked Guide me in the news-familiarity question
Played 12 months with choose-all-recommended plus the main call each month
Signed the ceasefire in month 12, read the verdict
scenarios.notes: Ended Mission complete, grade A, 688/1000. I knew at the end why: the Moments screen lists what went well and badly by month.

steps: Finished the whole Flashpoint without getting stuck
Used New game on the ranking screen to get back to the title
Started Hormuz Convoy as the United States and played month 1
scenarios.notes: Never blocked. Several moments of not trusting numbers (see friction, marked [trust]). Second game started cleanly.

friction.happened: The seed box only appears after pressing Play a seed, and the small grey arrow that starts it looks like decoration, not a button.

friction.where: Month 1 desk, free economic zone crisis
friction.expected: To understand each answer from its label
friction.happened: 'The free economic zone' meant nothing to me. 'Reject it and strike' sounds like a military strike and I did not know what I was rejecting. I picked it by accident (my tap landed on the wrong card), noticed on the next screen and kept it; it cost 1 capital.

friction.where: Desk, right panel: Choose all recommended
friction.expected: Everything the staff recommend, including the big crisis answer that carries a 'Recommended by...' label
friction.happened: It only takes meetings and routine orders. The main crisis card with a recommended answer stays open ('Nothing else to choose. Still open'). I pressed it every month and then had to press the crisis answer anyway. The label promises more than it does.

friction.where: Month 1, 'The move for your mission' centre vs right panel
friction.expected: [trust] One consistent Chief of Staff advice
friction.happened: [trust] Centre: Chief of Staff says Court United Kingdom. Right panel: 'Recommended by Chief of Staff' is National address. In game 2 month 1 the header says Chief of Staff: Reply via Muscat, the card says Chief of Staff recommends More escorts. I could not tell who recommends what or why.

friction.where: Mission line vs result card, months 5 and 9
friction.expected: [trust] The same number for US relations
friction.happened: [trust] Mission line: 'Keep Washington engaged: 39 to 48' while the card below says 'United States view of you 37 to 43'. Month 9: 46 to 60 vs 42 to 57.

friction.expected: [trust] 'You start next month with N' to be what I get
friction.happened: [trust] Month 1 panel said I would start next month with 5 before I added two more costs; month 3 panel said 4, I got 3. In month 9 picking an answer that costs 1 left the '0 left' line unchanged. The count moves as I click so I stopped trusting it.

From month 7 on the Next month / See your verdict button is cut off at the bottom edge at 1080 height (only its top strip shows), and a second clipped 'Next month' sits at the right edge of the newspaper page. Next month also opens the newspaper first, so I pressed it twice.

friction.expected: A new crisis in the finale
friction.happened: 'Energy price shock' came back with the same picture, the same -2.4% GDP and the same three answers as month 2. This is my round-1 deal-breaker, although the rest of the month was fresh.

friction.expected: A link to my earlier choice
friction.happened: 'Remember The plant at Enerhodar? Fuel prices hit record high in Ukraine' ties two unrelated things.

[trust] Header Score fell from 100 to 89 all game while every goal was 'on track', then the end screen gave 688/1000 and grade A. The last card said 'Heading to 112 if nothing changes' which made me doubt which number counts.

friction.expected: To find the same things as the desk
friction.happened: The left panel kept the decision, so I could do everything there. But the globe has about 40 unlabeled round icons I could not tell apart, and it turned to the US by itself in month 5, losing Ukraine. I did not press any marker; it looks like decoration, and I hovered a country name and the globe spun.

friction.expected: One obvious way to play again
friction.happened: Four choices: Replay same opening, New world, Compare runs (greyed), New game (plain text, no button look). I pressed New game because of the word; it went to the title screen, which was clear.

Unknown to me: Chancellor Merz, Frederiksen, Carney, Takaichi, Erdogan, a UK Prime Minister Burnham, IAEA at Enerhodar, Muscat, IRGC, fortress belt, mobilisation age. The dotted underlines and 'i' chips existed; I did not tap them. Guide me did keep the crisis texts short.

friction.where: Months 3, 7 and 9, 'The move for your mission'
friction.happened: Court United Kingdom was recommended while UK relations were already near the target ('keep the margin'); several months this step was one order or Hold, so I held and felt I was skipping the point.

Compare the Chief of Staff line in the centre with the 'Recommended by Chief of Staff' block in the right panel

suggestions.what: Make 'Choose all recommended' include the big crisis answer when it is recommended, or rename it to say it only takes routine staff picks
suggestions.goal_served: Never needs a manual; the screen tells her what to do next

suggestions.what: Keep the Next month button pinned at the bottom of the screen on result cards
suggestions.goal_served: Finish a Flashpoint in one sitting without hunting for buttons

suggestions.what: Show one US relation number everywhere (mission line and result card)
suggestions.goal_served: Understand why she won or lost

suggestions.what: Do not repeat a crisis within one Flashpoint
suggestions.goal_served: Avoid her round-1 deal-breaker, repeated cards

suggestions.what: On the ranking screen make one 'Play again' button primary and the others small
suggestions.goal_served: A clear way back after the end

delight: Result cards with an illustration, a quote from the street and a big number (shots/maya-desk/010-m1r.png, 017-m3r.png): each month feels like a small scene.
The Moments screen listing what went well and badly by month gave me the 'why I won' I wanted (053-mom.png).
'How you were seen': 'The country came round: 56% to 78%' (055-seen.png).
Achievements with rarity, and 'Beat 688 next time' on the ranking screen (052-rev3.png, 058-rank.png).
Memory of earlier choices: 'Remember The manpower wall? Hundreds of thousands march on Ukraine's capital' (032-m8r.png).

fun.reason: The scenes and the consequences of my choices (lowering the draft age cost 12 approval, the ceasefire cost 8) were fun; the repeated Choose-all and Execute routine in the middle months felt like clicking through.

clarity.reason: I always knew the next step until the button was cut off, and the end screens explained the win. Who recommends what, numbers that disagree and unknown names slowed me down.

visual.reason: Handsome result cards and title globe; the desk is dense with small text and the map has many unlabeled icons.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Result scenes, stamps ('Step achieved', 'Comeback'), grade and ladder feel like a game; the desk itself feels like paperwork.

agency.reason: Never fully blocked, but I could not see why Choose all recommended skipped the main call, and two recommendations contradicted each other.

realism.reason: Believable beats (draft age protests, US trade pact), but the same energy crisis twice broke it.

replay.reason: Seed code, replay same opening and a ladder to climb invite another run; I started Hormuz Convoy straight away.

recommend.reason: I finished in one sitting, won, and knew why. It took longer than my 15 minutes. I would tell a friend, with the warning that the middle months repeat.

verbatim: I did win and I know why, but half the time I was just pressing Choose all and Execute and hoping.
